title: Reductive groups over arbitrary scheme bases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H\to S$ an $S$-group scheme, that is, a group object in the category of schemes over $S$, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Use smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and the scheme-morphism conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], in particular finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Call $H$ reductive over $S$ if $H\to S$ is smooth affine of finite presentation and, for every algebraically closed field $k$ and every $s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$, the pullback group $H_s$ with its induced group law [def-pc-base-change] is reductive in the field sense [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. Thus its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. No nonemptiness or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1, printed p.81; smooth affine finite-presentation convention of lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group.
